summary: Safe de-optimization via snapshots and staged toggles for batching/caching/quant profiles
description:
Issue summary:
Customer applied a new set of optimizer heuristics (aggressive batching, prefix KV prefetch, and a quant profile optimized for 4-bit) via the console feature flag. After the change they observed a 95th/99th percentile tail latency increase and intermittent 5xx errors in the dedicated pool. Customer wants prescriptive steps to back out to a safe state without losing traffic or causing a multi-model rollout impact.

Impact:
- Production latency P95 increased from ~120ms to ~420ms for gptx-13b-q4_0 on dedicated pool us-east.
- Sporadic 502/504 seen at the API layer for long-context requests.
- High CPU on scheduler proxies due to larger batching and backpressure.
- Business impact: several internal apps experiencing degraded UX; classed as P1 for the customer.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: lexah-health-dedicated-us-east
- Runtime version: runtime-2.8.1-prod
- Feature flags applied: optimizer:aggressive-batching=v2, kv_prefetch=on, quant_profile=4bit_agile
- Observed on both gptx-13b-q4_0 and gptx-8b-fp16 model endpoints.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Toggle optimizer:aggressive-batching=v2 on the dedicated pool via Console -> Optimizer -> Flag overrides.
2) Turn on kv_prefetch and apply quant_profile=4bit_agile.
3) Run internal test harness (lexa-load test) at sustained 40 rps.
4) Observe tail latency jump within 5-10 minutes.

Observed behavior:
- Within minutes of toggling, average batch size climbed from 8 -> 22.
- Node-level GPU memory usage rose and some processes started to thrash leading to 502s.
- KV cache hit rate decreased for long-prefix requests due to prefetching thrash.

Expected behavior:
- Gradual batching increases with steady P99 latency guardrails and no 5xx spike.

Attachments / logs:
- Customer attached sample request IDs and trace links (included below in comments).
- Relevant dashboards: 
  - Serving runtime tail latency: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/serving/tail-latency?pool=lexah-health-dedicated-us-east
  - Batch size distribution: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/serving/batch-dist
  - KV cache metrics: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/serving/kv-cache

Requested outcome:
- Step-by-step safe procedure to move the dedicated pool to a conservative config with minimal traffic disruption.
- Recommended snapshot/restore use and guidance on staged toggles (what to change first, how long to observe, thresholds to stop).

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: aggressive-batching v2 increases dynamic max_batch_size too aggressively for long-context traffic; scheduler proxies queue longer causing backpressure.
KV cache hit rate drop suggests prefetch churn; prefetch may be evicting useful prefixes for long-running conversations.
Trace inspection (rq_7f2e1): saw GPU kernels experiencing spikes in activation memory and longer kernel compiles on quantized path for some requests.
Checked node metrics: one node showed repeated OOM-kill of helper process around incident times; correlates with increased batch sizes.
Console snapshot taken: snapshot_id=snap-20260313-1012. Recommended to use the snapshot for rollback if staged changes fail.
Suggested immediate metric thresholds to halt staged changes: P95 > 250ms OR 5xx rate > 0.5% over 5m OR batch_size_mean > 16 for 3 consecutive 1m buckets.
Related internal ticket INT-4402 includes a small scheduler bug fix that will be part of follow-up but is not safe to push during recovery window.
resolution: Mitigation plan executed: applied conservative overrides in the following order during low-traffic window: (1) disable kv_prefetch, (2) set optimizer:aggressive-batching=v2 -> v1-conservative, (3) revert quant_profile to baseline 8bit_mixed. Observed P95 revert to ~140ms and 5xx drop to baseline. Snapshot snap-20260313-1012 retained. Customer confirmed service usable. Plan documented in runbook and follow-ups scheduled.
